name: Mid-century modern product
summary: Post-war household objects of moulded plywood, fibreglass, steel rod and enamel, in organic curves and bright accents, made by American furniture firms and small Italian workshops.

philosophy.core_thesis: New materials from the war economy make a new kind of object: light, curved, bright and cheap enough for the new suburban home.
design_principles: Mould plywood, fibreglass or plastic in a compound curve that fits the body.
Put each shell on a slim base of steel rod, dowel or tapered wood, 10 to 25 mm in section.
Use organic outlines: the kidney, the boomerang, the egg and the disc.
Combine warm walnut or teak with a cool part of chrome, brass or enamel.
Add one saturated colour, in orange, turquoise, mustard or red, to each room set.
Make each object a module of a system that a customer can combine and extend.
Design the object for series production in a factory, and show the production method in the form.
Use a gloss finish of 40 to 80 GU on moulded and enamelled parts.
anti_patterns: Period revival ornament and carved legs
Heavy dark upholstery with a button back
Raw, unfinished wood without a clear shape
Stacks of small ornaments on a sideboard
A full range of pastel and grey only
Thick square legs and boxy frames

form.geometry: Compound curves and plane forms: the shell, the kidney, the boomerang and the saucer, on thin straight or splayed legs.
form.silhouette: An organic body that floats on a thin, spidery base; the leg angle is 5 to 15 degrees from the vertical.
form.edges: Soft radius of 10 to 40 mm on shells and tops; thin steel and wood parts keep a small radius of 1 to 3 mm.
form.proportion: A lounge seat is 38 to 42 cm high; a coffee table is 38 to 45 cm high with a top of 90 to 150 cm; a sideboard is 70 to 80 cm high on legs of 15 to 20 cm.
form.ornament: Pure shape and colour. The only repeated detail is a row of balls, a rod grid or a perforated pattern.
rules: Each shell or top has a curve in two directions or a free-form outline.
Each base is a rod, a dowel or a tapered leg of 10 to 25 mm section.
Each room set has one saturated colour that covers about 10% to 20% of the objects.
Wood is walnut, teak or birch with an oiled or lacquered finish.
A moulded shell is of one material in one piece.

materials.rule: Wood and moulded shells make about 60% of the visible surface; metal rods, glass and enamel make the rest.

finish.gloss: 40–80 GU on shells and enamel; 5–15 GU on oiled wood
finish.patina: The style wants clean, fresh surfaces; light wear on wood and leather is fine, but a chipped enamel or a dull shell is out of character.

hardware.section: Rod 6–12 mm for bases and frames; brass or steel legs 12–25 mm
hardware.joints: Welded steel rod, rubber shock mounts and visible bolts between shell and base.
hardware.handles: A routed finger pull, a round wooden knob of 30 mm, or a thin brass rod.
hardware.switches_and_taps: A plain ivory rocker switch; a chrome lever mixer with a slim, curved spout.

palette.strategy: Warm walnut and teak, plus one saturated colour: orange, turquoise, mustard or red; white and black as the ground.

processes: moulding of plywood under heat and pressure
manufacture.scale: Large series from American furniture firms and short series from Italian workshops, many with a design range from 1 to 10 thousand pieces.
manufacture.signs: Rubber shock mounts, spot welds, a rod frame, a split plywood back, and a maker's label under the seat.

objects.form: chrome lever with a slim, curved spout
plain rocker plate in ivory plastic
saucer or cone shade on a thin cord
long low credenza with doors on a track and splayed legs
moulded plywood seat and back on a steel rod base
enamelled pot with a wooden handle in a bright colour
wall clock with ball markers on thin brass rods

emotion.target_response: Optimism: the object looks new, light and a little playful, like a promise of a better home.

use_cases: furniture and accessories for a retro-modern home
a still life with a shell chair, a clock and a pendant lamp
product briefs for a mid-century reissue
a hardware schedule for a period house
avoid_when: The brief asks for a calm, grey, grid-based object set.
The brief asks for hand-made craft with a visible tool mark.

modifiers.how: Drop the saturated colour and the plastic, and use solid teak, bent birch and undyed wool.
Swap curves for a grid, and organic shapes for white and grey modules.
Use full plastic bodies, round pods and saturated colour on all large surfaces.

era_blend.note: A new object in a moulded shell on a slim base still belongs to the style.
